items.text: In blood samples from emergency and acute care patients, is collection through a peripheral intravenous catheter, compared with venepuncture, associated with more haemolysis, and does the association differ by tube type, catheter gauge, collector training and transport?
items.population: Blood samples from adults and children in emergency or acute care
items.intervention: Collection through a peripheral intravenous catheter (exposure)
items.outcome: Haemolysis defined by analyser index or visual inspection; sample rejection

finer: Feasible within 80 hours with librarian support if restricted to comparative studies; interesting to the emergency and laboratory directors; novel in its focus on technique subgroups; ethical as a literature review; relevant because it decides a joint policy.
summary: One PECO question with pre-specified effect modifiers.
